findings.reason: §11 must cite the landed owners and scope itself to the only delta not present (hold-or-divert versus today's refusal), or a node will reimplement a guard and a classifier a peer commit added the same day.
findings.text: §11 presents two repairs as new (detect a held member session before launching; make observe read stderr.log when the stream is empty), but both are already implemented: node.py:357 member_in_flight_verdict/refuse_member_in_flight detects a live member writer and is called at dispatch.py:6911, and dispatch.py:7817 _empty_stream_launch_failure already reads a zero-byte stream's stderr and sets phase launch-failed at dispatch.py:10874

findings.reason: the guard has one owner, so the plan should change what that guard does on a positive verdict (hold or divert rather than refuse) instead of adding a parallel detect that drifts from it.
findings.text: §11's first repair re-proposes member-session detection that member_in_flight_verdict/refuse_member_in_flight already own and that dispatch.py:6911 already calls; the seeded silent death is exactly the case node.py:298-305 describes

findings.reason: the classification is owned and wired in dispatch.py, so §11 should verify it fires for the reuse case and add a test rather than specify a parallel reader.
findings.text: §11's second repair re-proposes reading stderr for an empty stream, which _empty_stream_launch_failure already does (guarded by a stream stat plus a non-empty stderr, recorded under launch_failures in the launcher's vocabulary)

findings.reason: the supervisor is a substantial behaviour with a naturally narrow interface, and dispatch.py already grows twice (§3 and §10); one supervisor module would hide it, as the plan already did for the sibling role in fleet_supervisor.py.
findings.text: the plan places the whole per-run supervisor in dispatch.py as a scatter of module-level helpers (_supervisor_spec, _supervisor_argv, _start_supervisor, _spawn — the supervisor's spec, spawn, snapshot, exit record and _run_supervisor; roughly 1,800 lines inside a 12,471-line module) rather than one module whose interface is the spec in and exit.json out

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the per-run supervisor's behaviour is spread across ~15 module-level helpers inside the already 12,471-line reckon/crew/dispatch.py plus a 32-line entry shim, so no one module hides the supervision behind its interface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §11 would add a second detection guard beside node.py's and a second stderr reader beside dispatch.py's, naming no owner to extend, though both already have owners.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §11 states detecting a held member session and reading a silent launch's stderr as new work, but both exist already (node.py:member_in_flight_verdict, dispatch.py:_empty_stream_launch_failure, landed 2026-10-04 in 53eba38f2).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — each thin layer states why the machinery beneath cannot be used directly: supervisor_main.py exists to avoid runpy's duplicate-import warning (stated in the module and _supervisor_argv), and bin/fleet-supervisor is a launcher that execs reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py.
